rationale: State: trial-1bfb948628-param-aba0ae1b (BN fold + fused conv(+relu)/conv(+add+relu) epilogues) was accepted at objective 3.4129 ms vs parent 3.6579 ms (decision accepted, quality pass, paired gains 0.235/0.255 ms over MAD noise bounds 0.017/0.009 ms), and the current revision a345441f already carries it, so the next candidate must build on that implementation, not repeat it. Measured evidence on this exact version (observations/current/nsys-9ed9145c.json, single leased GPU-6c11763a, 46/46 kernels associated): GPU kernel busy is 3228.4 us across 46 kernels while the kernel span is 3778.3 us - 549.2 us of GPU-idle launch gaps sit inside one invocation (top gaps 225.6 us after max_pool before stage 2, 72.6, 48.8, 45.5, 33.2, 21.0, 19.9, 18.8, 15.3, 15.2 us mid-stream), i.e. the host periodically starves the GPU between kernels; against the clean objective 3.4129 ms the residual non-kernel overhead is ~0.185 ms. python_runtime-aea48e29 corroborates the shape: conv dispatch self time 0.867 ms (9x cudnn_convolution_relu 0.437, 8x cudnn_convolution_add_relu 0.296, 3x conv2d 0.134) plus 0.057 ms binding dispatch over 12 module sites, mostly hidden under GPU execution but surfacing as exactly those gaps. Remaining kernel work is dominated by 20 conv main kernels (2932.7 us, ~50 TFLOP/s FP32 - well-served by the current NCHW scudnn/winograd engines), then aten::max_pool2d at 189.2 us whose CUDA kernel max_pool_forward_nchw<float,int> also writes a 32x64x56x56 int32 indices tensor (~25.5 MB, half the kernel's store traffic) that nothing in this inference workload ever reads, and 19 cudnn per-conv auxiliary kernels (10x computeOffsets 13.1 us + 9x generateWinogradTiles 63.2 us = 76.3 us) that exist only to feed the eager per-call conv engines. Scope choice: these three levers (single whole-forward replay, pooling kernel, network-wide layout) each require owning the entire forward from the stem conv input through the classifier - pooling layout changes propagate into every residual and the head flatten, and replay must bracket the whole kernel sequence - so partial boundaries would insert per-boundary transposes or leave launch gaps between boundaries. The coherent editable boundary is the single module group eca3643289778aea5af3 (ResNetForImageClassification.forward, phase forward, observed call f2cf62caf57ad09f5d2f36aa): run() still calls model(pixel_values=pixels).logits through this one boundary under the legacy direct-callable backend, the region explicitly replaces the whole earlier bundle trial-1bfb948628-param-aba0ae1b (re-implementing its accepted folded/fused conv sites unchanged inside), and after that whole-bundle replacement no inherited required calls remain, so the boundary call itself carries coverage on every invocation. Everything inside the boundary is re-issued by the replacement: stem fused conv+relu, indices-free pooling, the 8 basic-layer and 3 shortcut sites, adaptive avg pool, flatten and the classifier GEMM. Single-device task: no communication buckets exist (communication-ownership.json buckets empty, not_applicable), so no cross-group attribution is claimed.
hypothesis: Primary mechanisms, both testable against paired AB/BA measurement: (1) Whole-region CUDA-graph replay - on the first legitimate invocation (warmup) run the accepted implementation eagerly once (warming/compiling every kernel), then capture the graph inside the actual adapter invocation context and replay on every subsequent invocation, so the measured unit becomes one graph launch executing the identical accepted kernels on current inputs (state['pixels'] storage is stable; verify at build, else copy into a static input buffer each invocation, ~30-40 us D2D for 19.3 MB). This should remove most of the ~0.185 ms clean-run residual between the 3.4129 ms objective and 3.228 ms kernel busy, plus whatever smaller starvation the clean run still exhibits; expectation ~0.10-0.19 ms. (2) Indices-free exact max pooling - replace the aten::max_pool2d site with a deterministic kernel computing the same 3x3/stride-2 max without materializing the ~25.5 MB int32 index tensor; max selection is exact (no accumulation), so selected values and downstream logits are unchanged bit-for-bit on the same layout; measured kernel is 189.2 us and roughly half its traffic is index stores, expected save ~0.08-0.12 ms. Combined expectation ~3.10-3.23 ms (5-9% off 3.4129 ms), 5-15x the 0.009-0.017 ms MAD noise bounds, with images_per_second rising above the current 9370/9382 (floor 7150). Optional route parameter, explicitly uncertain: channels_last/NHWC execution of the whole network (one input permute; all intermediates NHWC), which would also drop the 76.3 us of per-conv auxiliary kernels and possibly pick faster engines - but the current NCHW winograd/scudnn kernels already run near ~50 TFLOP/s FP32 and NHWC-FP32-without-TF32 engine availability on cudnn 9.20 per shape is unverified, so this route is a measured either/or never an assumption. Numerics and policies: replay re-executes the accepted kernels unchanged (bitwise-identical logits per invocation, so observe()'s repeated-forward closeness and exact top-1 hold trivially); indices-free pooling preserves exact max values; the NHWC route (if taken) reorders FP32 accumulation like the accepted BN fold did (~1e-7 relative, far inside atol=rtol=1e-4) and must pass the same full-logits/exact-top1 gates. TF32 stays disabled, cudnn.benchmark stays False, dtype/eval/inference_mode unchanged; the frozen batch is read from request state, never embedded. Risks to be resolved on the framework's GPU workers, each with the accepted guard-ladder pattern (installation probe, distinct route labels, per-site runtime latch): cudnn/cublas workspace capture behavior (graph pool; fall back to kernel-for-kernel eager replay of the accepted implementation = zero-change route); capture-context correctness per the binding contract (capture must record the replacement's own ops during a real invocation, never the original parent's work outside that context); Triton 3.7.1 compile-before-capture ordering; peak_allocated_bytes may rise slightly from the graph's static pool - it stays a non-objective metric under the 0.95 throughput floor. These expectations are hypotheses from diagnostic CUDA durations and gap measurements, not clean-timing results; the framework's independent paired measurement decides acceptance.
